landmarks.name: Society for Neuroscience · Major Brain Landmarks

hpa.name: NIDDK · Adrenal hormones and their control

regions.name: Frontal lobe
regions.detail: Includes areas involved in complex thinking and voluntary movement. Planning depends on connections with other regions.
regions.clue: I sit toward the front and include areas involved in planning.

regions.name: Parietal lobe
regions.detail: Helps combine sensory information and supports spatial processing. It works with other cortical areas.
regions.clue: Near the top, I help combine sensory and spatial information.

regions.name: Occipital lobe
regions.detail: Contains major visual-processing areas at the back of the cerebrum. Seeing also involves other regions.
regions.clue: At the back of the cerebrum, I contain major visual-processing areas.

regions.name: Temporal lobe
regions.detail: Includes areas involved in hearing. Deeper temporal structures also contribute to memory and emotional learning.
regions.clue: At the side, I include important hearing-related areas.

regions.name: Cerebellum
regions.detail: Helps coordinate movement and balance. It is not the sole source of movement commands.
regions.clue: Behind the brainstem, I help coordinate movement and balance.

regions.name: Brainstem
regions.detail: Contains circuits important for breathing and heart-rate regulation, and pathways between brain and body.
regions.clue: I connect toward the spinal cord and contain vital automatic-control circuits.

regions.name: Corpus callosum
regions.detail: A large bundle of nerve fibers linking the two cerebral hemispheres. It is not their only connection.
regions.clue: I am a large fiber bridge between the two cerebral hemispheres.

regions.name: Thalamus
regions.detail: A major relay for many sensory signals traveling to the cortex. Different thalamic nuclei have different roles.
regions.clue: Deep inside, I relay many sensory signals toward the cortex.

regions.name: Hypothalamus
regions.detail: Helps regulate temperature, hunger, thirst, sleep, and pituitary activity.
regions.clue: Below the thalamus, I help regulate temperature and hormone signaling.

regions.name: Pituitary gland
regions.detail: Its anterior part releases ACTH, which signals the adrenal glands to produce cortisol.
regions.clue: A gland beneath the brain, I release ACTH into the bloodstream.

regions.name: Hippocampus
regions.detail: Contributes to forming memories of events and their context. Memory is distributed across multiple systems.
regions.clue: I help form new memories of events and their context.

regions.name: Amygdala
regions.detail: Helps link significance and emotion with experiences. It works in networks, rather than acting as a single fear switch.
regions.clue: I help connect experiences with emotional significance.

myths.claim: Cortisol is made in the amygdala.
myths.explanation: Cortisol is produced by the adrenal glands, outside the brain.

myths.claim: The pituitary sends ACTH signals to the adrenal glands.
myths.explanation: ACTH is one link in the hypothalamus–pituitary–adrenal pathway.

myths.claim: The corpus callosum is a large connection between the cerebral hemispheres.
myths.explanation: Its nerve fibers carry information between hemispheres.

myths.claim: The cerebellum contributes to balance and coordinated movement.
myths.explanation: Movement coordination is one of its major roles.

myths.claim: Every function can be assigned to exactly one brain region.
myths.explanation: The structures in this atlas interact; a useful regional label is not a complete explanation of a behavior.

myths.claim: The hypothalamus helps regulate body temperature.
myths.explanation: Temperature regulation is one of several homeostatic functions it supports.
